module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 985

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/985](https://www.erdosproblems.com/985)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos985

/--
Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q \leq p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_985 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (p : ℕ) (hp_prime : p.Prime) (hp_nontrivial : p ≠ 2),
    ∃ q, q.Prime ∧ q < p ∧ orderOf (q : ZMod p) = p - 1 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Artin conjectured that 2 is a primitive root for infinitely many primes $p$, which
-- Hooley proved assuming the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis.

/--
Heath-Brown proved that at least one of 2, 3, or 5 is a primitive root for infinitely many primes $p$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_985.variants.two_three_five_primitive_root :
    Set.Infinite
      {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧
      (orderOf (2 : ZMod p) = p - 1 ∨
       orderOf (3 : ZMod p) = p - 1 ∨
       orderOf (5 : ZMod p) = p - 1)} := by
  sorry

end Erdos985

findings.description: The docstring says “for every prime p”, whereas the theorem explicitly assumes `hp_nontrivial : p ≠ 2`. This exception is necessary: at p = 2, the only prime q ≤ p is 2, whose residue has multiplicative order 0, not p − 1 = 1. The Lean statement handles this boundary correctly; its docstring should mention it.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/985 likewise says “for every prime p, there is a prime q
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to ask about every prime p > 2, preferably using q < p to match the theorem and current source. Keep the Lean theorem unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The source says that one fixed member of {2,3,5} is a primitive root for infinitely many primes. Lean instead asserts infinitude of the primes for which at least one of the three is a primitive root.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing A_q = {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ orderOf (q : ZMod p) = p − 1}, the Lean set is A_2 ∪ A_3 ∪ A_5. A finite union is infinite exactly when at least one constituent is infinite. The exact equivalence with `∃ q ∈ ({2,3,5} : Finset ℕ), A_q.Infinite` was proved independently in the scratch file.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in either theorem. The answer slot has the correct scope and polarity. For prime p, p − 1 > 0, so the order condition forces invertibility and correctly expresses a primitive root; no additional coprimality hypothesis is missing. The bounds q ≤ p and q < p are equivalent under this condition. Independent proofs and boundary tests in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully without sorryAx dependencies, including the p = 2 obstruction, a witness at p = 3, and the Heath-Brown equivalence. Computable power tests found prime primitive roots for every odd prime below 50. Both status tags agree with the source.
